searched: Read the federal monthly generator file for September 2026 for every New Mexico plant and matched each to GEM, which found Pyramid, La Luz, Piñon and Milagro missing.
Read the Southwest Power Pool queue download, the Berkeley Lab queue file and the El Paso Electric queue list for every New Mexico gas request.

Read all six resource plans in full: PNM 2026, Southwestern Public Service 2026, El Paso Electric 2025, Tri-State 2023 with its 2026 adequacy table, Farmington 2022 and Los Alamos 2022 with its 2026 slides.
Read the data center permit harvest, the Crusoe, Greater Kudu, Site Layer and Project Jupiter permit documents and the Zenith Volts announcement.
Read the state permit harvest, the commission case harvest and the local records harvest for the leads.
Read the possible updates sheet's New Mexico rows and the captive LNG sheet, which has no New Mexico row.

Opened every power named site in the state permit data service, the ECHO power list, the pending and issued permit tables, the federal clearinghouse, the business registry and the newspaper notice site; four new sites became watch items.
meta.irp_summary: All six New Mexico resource plans were read in full. PNM's 2026 plan adds La Luz II, 40 megawatts in 2031, and a 172 megawatt proxy turbine in 2029, both added in this batch. Southwestern Public Service's 2026 plan puts its new gas turbines at Gaines County and Tolk in Texas, held in GEM under L100001082470. El Paso Electric, Tri-State, Farmington and Los Alamos plan no new gas in New Mexico in their preferred plans.

qa.question: Should the 172 megawatt gas request at the Reeves Substation be added as Reeves unit 4 now, or held until a filing names the plant?
qa.finding: The Berkeley Lab queue file lists IA-PNM-2025-20, 172 megawatts of gas at the Reeves Substation for January 2029, and PNM's 2026 plan carries a 172 megawatt proxy turbine in 2029 in every portfolio except Scenario 12. The Reeves plant agent advised holding it because it could not open the queue file.
qa.recommendation: Accept the unit 4 add as announced; if the 2029 to 2032 request for proposals picks another site, move the unit to that site.
qa.researcher_notes: Berkeley Lab file, sheet 03, row IA-PNM-2025-20. PNM 2026 plan, PDF page 177 for the proxy turbine and PDF page 264 for Scenario 12, which drops it. The three PNM 2023 plan placeholder plants in GEM (L100001082463, L100001082465, L100001082467) may overlap this unit; the plant agents for those records ask whether to cancel them.

verifications.note: Berkeley Lab interconnection queue file through 2025, sheet 03, PNM rows. Request IA-PNM-2025-20 is 172 megawatts of gas at the Reeves Substation, queued 2025-03-24, in service 2029-01-01. IA-PNM-2017-14 and IA-PNM-2020-05 are gas requests at San Juan.

PNM 2026 integrated resource plan. Table 1-6 on page 45 and the table on page 118 list La Luz II, natural gas, 40 megawatts, 2031, at the certificate step. Page 177 (printed page 162) says a new 172 MW combustion turbine is included as a proxy unit in 2029 in all portfolios.

qa.question: Is the 2031 La Luz II turbine the same unit the federal file lists as canceled or postponed?

qa.recommendation: Keep unit 2 as pre-construction for 2031 from the plan; search the commission's case list for the La Luz II certificate case number and add it to Status Detail.
qa.researcher_notes: The commission's online case system has no case caption naming La Luz in the docket harvest, so the certificate case number is not known yet.

qa.question: Did the Milagro turbines retire in 2016, as the federal file says, or stop in 2022, as the Southwest Power Pool study says?
qa.finding: The federal generator file for September 2026 puts Milagro Cogeneration Plant 54814 on its Retired sheet with March 2016. The Southwest Power Pool study for the 60 megawatt Milagro request says Harvest Midstream's two 30 megawatt turbines stopped in 2022 and will return through request FEUS-1 in June 2027.
qa.recommendation: Keep the add as mothballed with the 2022 step, since the owner plans a return; change to retired only if the owner withdraws FEUS-1.
qa.researcher_notes: Federal file, Retired sheet, plant 54814. Southwest Power Pool Milagro study, project description section on the first pages.

qa.question: Is queue request FEUS-4, 60 megawatts of gas near Bloomfield, the Saddle Butte Eastside plant?
qa.finding: The Southwest Power Pool queue lists FEUS-4 near Bloomfield without a project name. The Bureau of Land Management approved the Saddle Butte Eastside gas peaker right-of-way near Bloomfield on July 2, 2026, and Saddle Butte's Westside plant matches FEUS-2.
qa.recommendation: Treat FEUS-4 as Eastside and add 60 megawatts to the Eastside unit once a permit or the queue study names it.

qa.plant_name: PNM San Juan gas request IA-PNM-2014-02
qa.question: Does the 80 megawatt San Juan gas request IA-PNM-2014-02 belong to any plant GEM should hold?
qa.finding: The Berkeley Lab queue file lists IA-PNM-2014-02, 80 megawatts of gas at the PNM-GPD San Juan Unit 5 point, queued February 2014 with an executed agreement and an in-service date of March 2018. No plant was built there, and no permit or news names one.
qa.recommendation: Leave it out of GEM; it looks like an earlier San Juan replacement idea dropped before 2020, which is outside the period GEM tracks cancellations.
qa.researcher_notes: Berkeley Lab file, sheet 03, row IA-PNM-2014-02. The state permit harvest has no gas turbine permit at San Juan from that period.

newplants.researcher_notes: GEM does not list this plant. Greater Kudu LLC holds state air permit 7026 for its data center at 4250 Messenger Loop, Los Lunas, Valencia County. The 2021 application 7026M5, section 4.3.5.1, lists 118 total stationary diesel-fired emergency generators, each greater than 560 kW, so the fleet is at least about 66 megawatts and over the 50 megawatt threshold. It stays approximate until checked on a satellite image. Greater Kudu is not in the entity list and needs to be created. This answers row 339 of the possible updates sheet.

newunits.researcher_notes: The Berkeley Lab queue file through 2025, sheet 03, row IA-PNM-2025-20, lists 172 megawatts of gas at the Reeves Substation in Bernalillo County, queued March 24, 2025, in service January 1, 2029, in the transitional cluster. PNM's 2026 resource plan, PDF page 177 (printed page 162), says a new 172 MW combustion turbine is included as a proxy unit in 2029 in all portfolios, with the real choice left to a 2029 to 2032 all-source request for proposals. The size and year match. Neither document names Reeves as the plant, only the substation, so a question card asks Baird to confirm. The plant agent for Reeves could not open the Berkeley Lab file and advised waiting; it opened here.

milestones.note: The queue request was filed March 24, 2025.
